summary: Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Xuesong Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008). In 2015, Zhang held an attested post as associate professor at Renmin University of China.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Xuezhu Li studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University in 2011 and has served as a research associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2026).
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Active in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies, Yadi Qu studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).

Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington under scholars including Gregory Schopen, she has taught Indian Studies (attested 1995–2000) and held a professorship (attested 2026) at Hebrew University.

A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, Karunadasa earned a BA from the University of Ceylon and a PhD from London under David Friedman. He directed the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and held visiting professorships at Hong Kong, SOAS, Calgary, and Toronto.
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and sinology. Zhou earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hojin (attested 2003) and earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under Richard Gombrich.
Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in Tibetology who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London around 2001–2004 under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under Yongdong Shi and studied under the traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Yannick Laurent works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. In 2026, he is attested as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and holds a post at the University of Munich.
Yanpei was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu from circa 1935 to 1940 and under Yinshun from circa 1941 to 1945.
Yao Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and sinology who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku. Wang held a post as guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Tsai completed a PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2010).

Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes and the University of Virginia, later holding a Mellon postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis and a post at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011–2015).

Yaroslav Vasilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (circa 1961–1967). He held posts at Kunstkamera and the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1968), and at Saint Petersburg State University.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Nara studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at Calcutta. He served at Komazawa University from 1960 and later directed the Soto Zen Research Center (2000).

A Tibetologist and linguist, Nagano studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1983). He served as professor and professor emeritus at the National Museum of Ethnology, and held executive roles at NIHU and SOKENDAI.
A scholar of philosophy and sinology, Yasuhiko Sueki studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1971 to 1976. Around 2017, Sueki held the title of professor emeritus at Komazawa University.
